text: AgentTrust is an interoperable security gateway and policy enforcement system designed for autonomous AI agent runtimes (LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Assistants, and custom tool-calling agents). It establishes zero-trust capability boundaries, intercepts tool invocations before execution, mandates cryptographic human approvals on high-blast actions, and maintains an immutable, hash-linked audit ledger. +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ | Autonomous Agent Runtime | | (LangChain / CrewAI / AutoGen / OpenAI / Custom) | +------------------------------------+------------------------------------+ | | 1. Record Cryptographic Evidence +------------------------------------+------------------------------------+ | Verifiable Audit Engine | | | | [ SHA-256 Backward Hash Chaining ] -> [ Merkle Tree Inclusion Proofs ] | | [ ECDSA P-256 Checkpoints ] -> [ NIST PQC ML-DSA Attestation ] | +-------------------------------------------------------------------------+ Key Capabilities 1. Deny-by-Default Policy Engine Agents operate without ambient authority. Capabilities are granted explicitly via fine-grained pattern rules across action and resource dimensions ( document:read , finance:* , cloud:*:deploy ). Parent orchestrator agents can mint subagents with strictly attenuated permissions. Subagents cannot exceed the capability envelope or spend allocation of the delegating parent. Evaluates the real-world reversibility, sensitive target exposure, and financial scope of actions prior to execution ( $[0.0, 1.0]$ ). High-impact actions escalate automatically to human review. Approval tickets support signed callback links for Slack, Microsoft Teams, and email. Every approval generates a single-use cryptographic execution nonce that is burned atomically upon first presentation, preventing replay attacks (HTTP 409). Every event links to the preceding event hash ( prev_hash -> entry_hash ). The ledger tip is signed using asymmetric ECDSA P-256 and verified through periodic cryptographic checkpoints. Constructs binary Merkle trees over ledger events, allowing auditors to verify individual actions offline via cryptographic inclusion proofs without exposing proprietary database records. Traps rogue outbound network calls, blocking access to loopback interfaces, private RFC1918 CIDR blocks, and cloud instance metadata endpoints ( 169.254.169.254 , metadata.google.internal ). Compares an agent's stated mission against proposed tool arguments to detect mission deviation, prompt injection overrides, and exfiltration attempts pre-execution. Enforces spend caps and rate ceilings per execution run. If token or action velocity spikes unexpectedly ( $> 30\text{ RPM}$ ), the system trips an automatic circuit breaker. A global panic mechanism revoking all active agent credentials, invalidating pending nonces, and taking a forensic checkpoint in under 15 milliseconds. Pre-flight OpenQASM parsing enforcing hardware qubit bounds ( $< 127$ qubits) and coherence depth limits ( $< 500$ ). Emits dual classical and NIST FIPS 204 (ML-DSA / Dilithium) hybrid attestation envelopes to defend archives against future quantum adversaries.
